label: ass:class
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:class}
The integers $d,k\ge1$, the bounds $\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}}>0$ and $0<\lambda\le\Lambda$,
and the horizon $T>0$ are known to the algorithm. Every component of
$b$ and $\sigma$ belongs to $C_b^k([0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d)$, every time--space
derivative of total order at most $k$, including order zero, has absolute
value at most $\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}}$, and
\[
 \lambdaI_d\preceq a(t,z)\preceq\LambdaI_d,
 \qquad (t,z)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d.
\]
Derivatives at the time endpoints have continuous one-sided extensions.

label: cx:admissible
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{cx:admissible}
An admissible algorithm receives the class bounds, horizon, endpoint
data and requested grid, uses only the coefficient queries and
primitives specified in Section~\ref{sec:model}, and terminates almost
surely with an exact sample for every allowed choice of coefficients
and inputs in its target family. Its expected work may be infinite.
For fixed endpoints, define
\begin{align}
 \mathfrak R_F^x(T,m)
 &=\inf_A\sup_{\substack{(b,\sigma)\in\mathcal F_T\\
                         \mathbf t\in\mathcal G_F(T,m)}}
       \mathbb{E}_{b,\sigma}\mathcal{W}_A(T,x,\mathbf t),\nonumber\\
 \mathfrak R_B^{x,y}(T,m)
 &=\inf_A\sup_{\substack{(b,\sigma)\in\mathcal F_T\\
                         \mathbf t\in\mathcal G_B(T,m)}}
       \mathbb{E}_{b,\sigma}\mathcal{W}_A(T,x,y,\mathbf t).
 \label{cx:risks}
\end{align}
The infima are over admissible query-only algorithms for the respective
families. A single algorithm within each supremum must handle all
coefficients and grids in that supremum; it accesses the unknown
coefficients only through point queries.

title: Remark
body_md:
For bridges, the minimax optimality established here concerns the
number of requested observations $m$, with the horizon and endpoints
fixed. The construction also improves the dependence on the horizon
relative to the natural terminal-rejection method of
Section~\ref{br5:terminal-rejection}. For equal endpoints, that
method has worst-case expected work at least $c_1e^{c_2T}$, as
witnessed by an admissible constant-coefficient diffusion, whereas
our sampler has the uniform bound $O\{(1+T)^Q\log(3+T)+m\}.$
Thus the horizon dependence is polynomial up to a logarithmic
factor. The sharp minimax dependence on the bridge horizon remains
open and is a direction of future research.

label: supp:fw:retry
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{supp:fw:retry}
Conditional on a fixed history $\mathcal H$, let
$(C_k,S_k,Y_k)_{k\ge1}$ be independent identically distributed trial records,
where $C_k\ge0$ is the work of trial $k$, $S_k\in\{0,1\}$ indicates success (or not), and $Y_k$ is the proposed output. Suppose
$\mathbb{P}(S_k=1\mid\mathcal H)=q>0$ and
$\mathbb{E}(C_k\mid\mathcal H)\le c$. Then, for
$\nu=\inf\{k:S_k=1\}$, we have $\nu<\infty$ almost surely and $\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{k=1}^{\nu} C_k\,\middle|\,\mathcal H\right]\le c/q.$
The successful trial's output has the one-trial conditional law given
success.
head: environment
name: Work through the first successful trial

title: Proof
body_md:
Conditional on $\mathcal H$, $\nu$ is geometric with parameter $q$.
The event $\{\nu\ge k\}$ depends only on the first $k-1$ trials and is
conditionally independent of $C_k$. Then by the conditional Tonelli theorem, we have
\[
 \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{k\ge1}\mathbf{1}\{\nu\ge k\}C_k
       \,\middle|\,\mathcal H\right]
 =\sum_{k\ge1}(1-q)^{k-1}\mathbb{E}(C_k\mid\mathcal H)\le c/q.
\]
If $Y_k$ is the output in trial $k$, then for a measurable set $A$,
\[
 \mathbb{P}(Y_\nu\in A\mid\mathcal H)
 =\sum_{k\ge1}(1-q)^{k-1}
       \mathbb{P}(Y_k\in A,S_k=1\mid\mathcal H)
 =\mathbb{P}(Y_1\in A\mid S_1=1,\mathcal H),
\]which finishes the proof.

label: core:parametrix
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{core:parametrix}
\label{supp:core:parametrix}
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:class}, for every fixed
$T_{\mathrm{win}}>0$ there are computable constants $C_g,C_H,C_p^*>0$
such that, for $0<h=t-s\le\min\{T_{\mathrm{win}},T\}$,
\eqref{core:parametrix-series} converges absolutely to $p(e)$ and
\[
 g(e)\le C_gG_{\kappa,h}(w),\qquad
 |H(e)|\le C_Hh^{-1/2}G_{\kappa,h}(w),\qquad
 0\le R(e)\le C_p^*,\qquad \kappa=2\Lambda.
\]
The constants depend only on $d,\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}},\lambda,\Lambda,T_{\mathrm{win}}$.
As a result, the
Chapman--Kolmogorov identity holds pointwise.
head: environment
name: Parametrix representation

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $T_{\mathrm{win}}>0$ and restrict attention to $h\le\min\{T_{\mathrm{win}},T\}$.
Throughout the proof, we suppress the dependence of $C_H$ and $C_p^*$
on $T_{\mathrm{win}}$ in the notation.

The product rule gives $|\partial_\xi a_{ij}|\le2d\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}}^2$ for every
time or spatial coordinate $\xi$. Hence
\[
 |b(s,u)|\le B_b:=\sqrt d\,\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}},\qquad
 \|a(s,u)-a(t,v)\|_F\le L_a(h+|w|),
\] where $L_a:=2d^{5/2}\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}}^2.$
With $r=|w|/\sqrt h$ and $\kappa=2\Lambda$, ellipticity yields $\frac{g(e)}{G_{\kappa,h}(w)}\le C_g e^{-r^2/(4\Lambda)} \leq C_g,$ with $C_g:=\left(\frac{2\Lambda}{\lambda}\right)^{d/2}.$
Using $|A^{-1}w/h|\le r/(\lambda\sqrt h)$ in
\eqref{core:defect}, we obtain $|H(e)|\le h^{-1/2}P_{T_{\mathrm{win}}}(r)g(e),$ where
\[
 P_{T_{\mathrm{win}}}(r):=\frac{B_b}{\lambda}r+
 \frac{L_a}{2}(r+\sqrt{T_{\mathrm{win}}})
 \left(\frac{r^2}{\lambda^2}+\frac{\sqrt d}{\lambda}\right)
 =\sum_{j=0}^3\alpha_jr^j.
\]
Since $\sup_{r\ge0}r^je^{-r^2/(4\Lambda)}=(2j\Lambda/e)^{j/2}$
for $j\ge1$, the computable choice
\[
C_H:=C_g\left[\alpha_0+
\sum_{j=1}^3\alpha_j(2j\Lambda/e)^{j/2}\right]
\]
gives $g(e)\le C_gG_{\kappa,h}(w)$ and $|H(e)|\le C_Hh^{-1/2}G_{\kappa,h}(w).$

For a bounded Lipschitz function $f$ and time pair $q < t$, we denote $F_{t,f}(q,z)=\int g(q,z;t,v)f(v)\,\,\mathrm{d} v.$
Then we have
\begin{equation*}
 \sup_z|F_{t,f}(t-h,z)-f(z)|
 \le\sqrt h\left(C\|f\|_\infty+
 \sqrt{d\Lambda}\operatorname{Lip}(f)\right),
\end{equation*}
where $C$ depends only on $d,\lambda,\Lambda,L_a$.

For $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $s<\beta<t$, the initial-variable
derivatives of $F_{t,f}$ are bounded on $[s,\beta]\times\mathbb{R}^d$.
It\^o's formula and \eqref{core:defect} therefore imply
\[
 \mathbb{E} F_{t,f}(\beta,X_\beta)-F_{t,f}(s,u)
 =\int_s^\beta\int P_{s,u;q}(\,\mathrm{d} z)
       \int H(q,z;t,v)f(v)\,\,\mathrm{d} v\,\,\mathrm{d} q.
\]
The terminal approximation and continuity of $X$ identify the limit
of the left side as $\beta\uparrow t$. The absolute integral on the
right is at most $2C_H\sqrt h\,\|f\|_\infty$. Therefore, by Fubini's theorem and dominated convergence theorem, 
\begin{equation}\label{supp:ana:measure-duhamel}
 P_{s,u;t}(\,\mathrm{d} v)=\left[g(s,u;t,v)+
 \int_s^t\int H(q,z;t,v)P_{s,u;q}(\,\mathrm{d} z)\,\,\mathrm{d} q\right]\,\mathrm{d} v.
\end{equation}

For ordered times $s<q_1<\cdots<q_n<t$, set $q_0=s$, $q_{n+1}=t$
and $\Delta_i=q_{i+1}-q_i$.
Gaussian convolution in the definition of $K_n$, followed by the
Dirichlet integral, gives
\begin{align}
 \mathsf Z_n(h)
&=\int_{\substack{\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_n>0\\\Delta_1+\cdots+\Delta_n<h}}\prod_{i=1}^n\Delta_i^{-1/2}\,\,\mathrm{d}\Delta_1\cdots\,\mathrm{d}\Delta_n
   =\frac{\pi^{n/2}h^{n/2}}{\Gamma(1+n/2)}
 \label{supp:ana:term-bound}
\end{align} and $|K_n(e)|\le C_gC_H^n\mathsf Z_n(h)G_{\kappa,h}(w).$
In particular, all convolution integrals are absolutely convergent.
Iterating \eqref{supp:ana:measure-duhamel} gives
\[
 P_{s,u;t}(\,\mathrm{d} v)=
 \left[\sum_{n=0}^{m-1}K_n(s,u;t,v)+\mathcal R_m(s,u;t,v)\right]\,\mathrm{d} v,
 \qquad
 \|\mathcal R_m(s,u;t,\cdot)\|_1\le C_H^m\mathsf Z_m(h).
\]
Since $\frac{C_H^{n+2}\mathsf Z_{n+2}(h)}{C_H^n\mathsf Z_n(h)}
 =\frac{\pi C_H^2h}{1+n/2}\longrightarrow0,$
the remainder tends to zero and the series converges absolutely
and in $L^1(\,\mathrm{d} v)$.
Also, each $K_n$ is jointly continuous for $s<t$.
Then by the bound \eqref{supp:ana:term-bound} the parametrix series is locally uniformly convergent on $s<t$.
Its sum is therefore continuous and, by the vanishing remainder,
agrees with the continuous transition density at every endpoint: $p(e)=g(e)+\sum_{n\ge1}K_n(e).$
Hence,
$p=g+p\otimes H$ pointwise.

Finally, let $u_h=C_H\sqrt{\pi h}$. Splitting the series into even
and odd terms and using
$\Gamma(j+3/2)\ge(\sqrt\pi/2)j!$ gives $\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{u_h^n}{\Gamma(1+n/2)}
 \le(1+2u_h/\sqrt\pi)e^{u_h^2}.$
Consequently, with $u_*:=C_H\sqrt{\pi T_{\mathrm{win}}},$
$0\le R(e)\le C_p^*:=C_g(1+2u_*/\sqrt\pi)e^{u_*^2}.$
All constants depend only on $d,\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}},\lambda,\Lambda,T_{\mathrm{win}}$.
Taking $T_{\mathrm{win}}=1$ gives the constants used in the main text.
The Markov property implies the Chapman--Kolmogorov identity almost
everywhere in the final endpoint. Continuity and the Gaussian bound
make its integral continuous there, so the identity holds pointwise.

label: core:randomterm
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{core:randomterm}
For every $j\ge1$ and $0<h\le1$, a query-only construction generates
$\Upsilon_j$ satisfying \eqref{core:Tnproperties} in $O(j+1)$ work,
uniformly in the edge and coefficient instance.
head: environment
name: Randomized convolution term

label: core:randomgaps
title: Proof
body_md:
We first describe the algorithm, and then show that is satisfies \eqref{core:Tnproperties} with the work guarantee. Draw independent $U_0\sim\operatorname{Uniform}(0,1)$ and
$\chi_i\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)$, $1\le i\le j$, and set
\begin{equation}\label{core:randomgaps}
 Q_0=-\log U_0,\qquad Q_i=\chi_i^2/2\ (1\le i\le j),
 \qquad \Delta_i=\frac{hQ_i}{\sum_{l=0}^jQ_l}.
\end{equation}
On the null event that any gap is zero, return zero before forming
denominators. Otherwise the normalized gaps have the Dirichlet law
with parameters $(1,1/2,\ldots,1/2)$; their density on the gap simplex
is $\mathsf Z_j(h)^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^j\Delta_i^{-1/2}$.
Let $\tau_0=s$, $\tau_{i+1}=\tau_i+\Delta_i$, $z_0=u$ and
$z_{j+1}=v$. Conditional on the gaps, generate the intermediate
states of a Gaussian bridge with covariance parameter $\kappaI_d$.
Its joint density is
\[
 \frac{\prod_{i=0}^jG_{\kappa,\Delta_i}(z_{i+1}-z_i)}
 {G_{\kappa,h}(v-u)}.
\]
For an explicit implementation, draw $z_i$, $1\le i\le j$,
successively with conditional mean and covariance
\[
 z_{i-1}+\frac{\tau_i-\tau_{i-1}}{t-\tau_{i-1}}(v-z_{i-1}),
 \qquad
 \frac{(\tau_i-\tau_{i-1})(t-\tau_i)}{t-\tau_{i-1}}\kappaI_d.
\]
Writing $G_i=G_{\kappa,\Delta_i}(z_{i+1}-z_i)$, define
\begin{equation}\label{core:random-correction}
 \Upsilon_j=\mathsf Z_j(h)
 \frac{g(s,u;\tau_1,z_1)}{G_0}
 \prod_{i=1}^j
 \frac{\sqrt{\Delta_i}H(\tau_i,z_i;\tau_{i+1},z_{i+1})}{G_i}.
\end{equation}
Cancellation against the gap and bridge densities proves the
expectation in \eqref{core:Tnproperties}. The bounds of
Lemma~\ref{core:parametrix} applied to each factor give its pathwise
bound. Absolute integrability follows from the same bounds.

All gaps, bridge states and factors require $O(j+1)$ scalar work in
fixed dimension. The normalizers are evaluated without the Gamma
function using the quantity
\[
 \mathsf Z_0(h)=1,\qquad \mathsf Z_1(h)=2\sqrt h,
 \qquad \mathsf Z_{j+2}(h)=\frac{2\pi h}{j+2}\mathsf Z_j(h).
\]Therefore, the proof is finished.

label: core:localpositive
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{core:localpositive}
The local estimator $\hat{R}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is unbiased for $R(e)$
and has uniformly bounded expected work for $0<h\le1$.
For each $L\ge1$, there is a computable $h(L)>0$ such that
$h\le h(L)$ and $|w|\le L\sqrt h$ imply \eqref{core:localbounds}.
The work at selected order $J$ is $O(J+1)$.
head: environment
name: Local estimator

title: Proof
body_md:
Generate $J$ by counted fair-coin trials until the first success;
then $\mathbb{P}(J=j)=2^{-j}$ and $\mathbb{E} J=2$.
The absolute convolution bounds and
Lemma~\ref{core:randomterm} justify summing the conditional
expectations, giving $\mathbb{E}\widehat R_{\mathrm{loc}}=R(e)$.
They also give the asserted work bound.

For the pathwise assertion, ellipticity gives
\[
 r_0\ge\rho_L:=(\kappa/\Lambda)^{d/2}e^{-L^2/(2\lambda)}
 \quad\text{if }|w|\le L\sqrt h.
\]
Choose
\begin{equation*}
 \delta_L=\min\{1/2,\rho_L/(8C_g)\},\qquad
 h(L)=\min\{1,\delta_L^2/[4\pi(1+C_H)^2]\}.
\end{equation*}
Then $2C_H\sqrt{\pi h}\le\delta_L$. Since $J\ge1$ and
$\Gamma(1+J/2)\ge1/2$, \eqref{core:Tnproperties} yields
\[
 |2^J\Upsilon_J|
 \le\frac{C_g(2C_H\sqrt{\pi h})^J}{\Gamma(1+J/2)}
 \le2C_g\delta_L\le\rho_L/4\le r_0/4.
\]
Together with $r_0\le C_g$, this proves \eqref{core:localbounds}.

label: core:spatialguarantee
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{core:spatialguarantee}
With the choices in \eqref{core:envelope-calibration},
Algorithm~\ref{core:spatialalgorithm} is query-only, terminates almost
surely and satisfies
\[
 \mathbb{P}\{\operatorname{SpatialCoin}(e)=1\}=R(e)/C(\zeta),
 \qquad \mathbb{E} W_{\mathrm{sp}}(e)\le C_{\mathrm{sp}}<\infty,
\]where $C_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is a constant that depends only on $d,\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}},\lambda,\Lambda$ and the primitive costs.
The bound is uniform over the coefficient class, time locations and
endpoints with $0<t-s\le h_{\mathrm{env}}$. It also holds
conditionally when the input edge is determined by previous history
and the call uses fresh randomness.
head: environment
name: Spatial coin

title: Proof
body_md:
The choices of $b_{\mathrm{env}}$ and $h_{\mathrm{env}}$ imply
$0\le R(e)\le C(\zeta)$ and make the local uniform comparison valid.
Dividing the three terms of \eqref{core:midpoint-normalizer} by
$C(\zeta)\ge k_{\mathrm{env}}e^{a_0|\zeta|^2}$ bounds each by
$\eta/3$ whenever $|\zeta|>L_{\mathrm{env}}$. Thus every nonlocal
call branches with probability at most $1/4$.

Let $N_l$ be the number of calls at depth $l$, with $N_0=1$.
Conditional expectation gives
\[
 \mathbb{E} N_{l+1}\le\tfrac12\mathbb{E} N_l,\qquad
 \mathbb{E} N_l\le2^{-l},\qquad
 \mathbb{E}\sum_{l\ge0}N_l\le2.
\]
Consequently the recursion has finitely many calls almost surely.
Each call's own operations terminate almost surely and have uniformly
bounded conditional mean work: the local case costs $O(J+1)$ with
$\mathbb{E} J=2$, and the nonlocal case uses a bounded number of operations,
including the mixture draw. Charging a call only for its own work
and summing over depths therefore proves the uniform work bound.

For correctness, let $f(e)=R(e)/C(\zeta)$. The local output has mean
$f(e)$ by Lemma~\ref{core:localpositive}. On a nonlocal edge, write
$\widetilde\mathbb{E}$ for expectation under the tilted midpoint law. Therefore,
\[
 \frac{S(\zeta)}{C(\zeta)}\widetilde\mathbb{E}[f(e_1)f(e_2)]
 =\frac{\mathbb{E}[R(e_1)R(e_2)]}{C(\zeta)}=f(e).
\]
To avoid assuming correctness of the recursive outputs, truncate at
depth $l$ and replace unresolved calls by auxiliary coins of their
prescribed means $f$, independently conditional on their inputs.
Such coins are well defined because $0\le f\le1$. Backward induction
gives mean $f(e)$ for each truncated procedure. Couple it with the
full procedure using the same randomness before depth $l$. Their
outputs differ only if that depth is reached, with probability at
most $\mathbb{P}(N_l>0)\le2^{-l}$. Letting $l\to\infty$ proves the claim.
Fresh randomness gives the same argument conditionally on any
history determining the input edge.

label: core:shortcoin
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{core:shortcoin}
The transition coin algorithm is query-only, terminates
almost surely and satisfies \eqref{core:shortcoinlaw}. Its total
expected work is bounded by a class constant $C_{\mathrm{TC}}$,
uniformly over all edges of duration at most $h_{\mathrm{env}}$.
The same bound holds conditionally on the input edge.
head: environment
name: Transition coin

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $C(\zeta)\le A_0e^{a_0|\zeta|^2}$, the additional comparison
is valid. Independence and Lemma~\ref{core:spatialguarantee} imply
\[
 \mathbb{P}\{\operatorname{TransitionCoin}(e)=1\}
 =\frac{R(e)}{C(\zeta)}
   \frac{C(\zeta)}{A_0e^{a_0|\zeta|^2}}
 =\frac{p(e)}{E_h(w)}.
\]
The Gaussian identity \eqref{core:gaussianenvelope} follows from
$a_0=1/(8\kappa)$. The additional operations have bounded cost,
so the work and termination assertions follow from the spatial coin.

label: core:shorttransition
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{core:shorttransition}
The short transition algorithm in
Section~\ref{core:shorttransitionalgorithm} is query-only, terminates
almost surely and returns a state of density $p(s,u;t,\cdot)$.
Its expected total work, including all rejected trials, is uniformly
bounded over the coefficient class, starting states and intervals
with $0<t-s\le h_{\mathrm{env}}$. This bound holds conditionally on
the starting state and times.
head: environment
name: Short transition

title: Proof
body_md:
With $h=t-s$, the joint density of one proposal and acceptance is
\[
 G_{4\kappa/3,h}(v-u)\frac{p(s,u;t,v)}{E_h(v-u)}
 =\frac{p(s,u;t,v)}{K_{\mathrm{rej}}}.
\]
Each trial therefore succeeds with probability $1/K_{\mathrm{rej}}$,
and its conditional law given success is the required transition.
The Gaussian proposal and Lemma~\ref{core:shortcoin} give a uniform
bound $c_F$ on the mean work of one trial. Independent restarts and
Lemma~\ref{supp:fw:retry} bound the total expected work by
$c_0+K_{\mathrm{rej}}c_F$, where $c_0$ accounts for preliminary
operations.

label: br5:terminal-rejection-lower
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Cost of terminal rejection

title: Proof
body_md:
The Gaussian envelope implies that
\[
 p(T-\Delta,u;T,y)\le E_\Delta(y-u)
 =U_\Delta\exp\{-3|y-u|^2/(8\kappa\Delta)\}\le U_\Delta.
\]
Thus \eqref{br5:terminal-rejection-test} is implemented by a
transition coin and an independent comparison with the displayed
exponential. Multiplication by the unconditional prefix density gives the
unnormalized bridge density divided by $U_\Delta$. By the
Chapman--Kolmogorov identity, its mass is $p(0,x;T,y)/U_\Delta$.
Conditioning on acceptance gives the bridge law, and independent
restarts give the stated mean trial count.

Since the coefficient class is nonempty, choose an admissible
diffusion coefficient $\sigma_*$ and fix a point $(t_*,z_*)$ in its
domain. Set $\Sigma_0=\sigma_*(t_*,z_*)$. This constant matrix
inherits the componentwise and ellipticity bounds of $\sigma_*$.
Choose the constant coefficients
\[
 b(t,z)\equiv\mu:=\frac{\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}}}{2}e_1,\qquad
 \sigma(t,z)\equiv\Sigma_0,\qquad
 A:=\Sigma_0\Sigma_0^\top,
\]
where $e_1$ is the first coordinate vector. These coefficients
satisfy the original assumptions, with all positive-order
derivatives equal to zero. For equal endpoints, their transition
density is
\[
 p(0,x;T,x)=(2\pi T)^{-d/2}(\det A)^{-1/2}
             \exp\{-T\mu^\top A^{-1}\mu/2\}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \mathbb{E}\nu_{\mathrm{tr}}
 =A_0\sqrt{\det A}\,\kappa^{-d/2}M^{d/2}
            e^{T\mu^\top A^{-1}\mu/2}
 \ge A_0(2\lambda/\kappa)^{d/2}
            e^{\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}}^2T/(8\Lambda)},
\]
using $M\ge2$, $\det A\ge\lambda^d$ and
$A^{-1}\succeq\Lambda^{-1}I_d$.
Each trial incurs at least a fixed positive primitive cost
$c_{\min}$, so
$\mathcal{W}_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge c_{\min}\nu_{\mathrm{tr}}$ pathwise.
Taking expectations proves the claimed work lower bound.
head: environment

label: br5:cell-counts
title: Proof
body_md:
Consider steps~2--6 on $[0,2n]$, with zero endpoints. Let $m'$ be
the number of requested times for this construction, including the
midpoint $n$. The number of retained cells and the maximum number
of good neighbors satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{br5:cell-counts}
 S_{\mathrm{cell}}=O(n^{d(3+4/\alpha)}),\qquad
 K_{\mathrm{nb}}=O(n^{d(1+4/\alpha)}),
\end{equation}
since $R\asymp n$, $N\asymp n^4$, $h\asymp n^{-3}$,
$L\asymp n^{-1}$ and $\ell\asymp n^{-2-4/\alpha}$.
Enumerating the integer offsets of length at most $L/\ell$ at each
cell and time layer constructs the cell graph and its known factors
in $O(NS_{\mathrm{cell}}K_{\mathrm{nb}})$ work. The augmented graph
therefore has
$E=O(NS_{\mathrm{cell}}K_{\mathrm{nb}}+N^2+dN)$ edges.

Lemma~\ref{br5:global-guarantee} combines the graph draw and the
selected component's proposal and acceptance test. It gives an exact
coarse bridge with expected work at most
\[
 C\{EN^3\log(4EN)+N^2+n+NS_{\mathrm{cell}}\}
 =O\{n^Q\log(2n)\}.
\]
Here $N^4S_{\mathrm{cell}}K_{\mathrm{nb}}=O(n^Q)$,
$N^5=O(n^{20})=O(n^Q)$ and $\log(4EN)=O(\log(2n))$.
The $n^{20}$ term is absorbed since $d\ge1$ and $0<\alpha\le1$.
Constructing the graph and storing and updating the sampled
states also require at most $O(n^Q\log(2+n))$ work.
Lemma~\ref{br5:insertion} preserves the bridge law and adds
$O(m'+N)$ expected work. Thus the total work $\mathcal{W}_0$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{bridge:calibrated-summary}
 \mathbb{E}\mathcal{W}_0\le C\{n^Q\log(2n)+m'\}.
\end{equation}
All implementations use only coefficient values and the stated
primitives.

For general inputs, use the fixed constant
\begin{equation}\label{br:scale-constant}
 L_{\mathrm{sc}}=\max\left\{1,\frac{2+\sqrt d}{4},
                              \frac{(\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}}+1)^2}{2\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}}^2}\right\}.
\end{equation}
Write $D_{\mathrm{end}}=|y-x|$ and $H=H_{T,x,y}$.
The inequalities $H\ge T$, $H\ge D_{\mathrm{end}}^2/T$ and
$H\ge2D_{\mathrm{end}}$ imply
\[
 r\le(2L_{\mathrm{sc}})^{-1},\qquad
 D_{\mathrm{end}}/S\le(4L_{\mathrm{sc}})^{-1},\qquad
 D_{\mathrm{end}}/\sqrt{TS}\le(2L_{\mathrm{sc}})^{-1/2}.
\]
For a scalar coefficient component $f$ and $p+|\beta|\le k$,
the chain rule gives
\begin{equation}\label{br:affine-derivatives}
 \left|\partial_s^p\partial_z^\beta
 f(rs,x+(s/S)w+\sqrt r\,z)\right|
 \le\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}}\left(r+\frac{\|w\|_1}{S}\right)^p r^{|\beta|/2}
 \le\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}},
\end{equation}
because $r+\|w\|_1/S\le(2+\sqrt d)/(4L_{\mathrm{sc}})\le1$.
Positive-order derivatives of $\widetilde b$ have the additional
factor $\sqrt r\le1$, while
$|\widetilde b_i|\le(\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}}+1)/\sqrt{2L_{\mathrm{sc}}}\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}}$.
The transformed covariance is the original covariance evaluated
at the transformed point, so the ellipticity bounds are unchanged.
The one-sided derivative conventions at the time endpoints are
also preserved. Together with the coefficient and derivative
bounds established above, these facts show that the transformed
coefficients satisfy Assumption \ref{ass:class} on $[0,S]$.

Brownian scaling gives \eqref{br:affine-coefficients}. With
$\Psi_s(z)=x+(s/S)w+\sqrt r\,z$, the continuous densities satisfy
\[
 \widetilde p(s,z;q,\zeta)
 =r^{d/2}p(rs,\Psi_s(z);rq,\Psi_q(\zeta)),\qquad s<q.
\]
Change of variables yields this identity almost everywhere, and
continuity extends it to every endpoint. If $n$ was added to the
requested grid, first integrate out its state by the
Chapman--Kolmogorov identity. Substitution into the bridge density
for the remaining $m$ times gives the factor $r^{md/2}$, exactly
the Jacobian of \eqref{br:affine-output}. Hence the returned states
have the target bridge distribution.

Each transformed scalar query uses one original query and $O(d)$
arithmetic, with time arguments in $[0,T]$. Parameter and grid
processing cost $O(n+m)$, and $m'\le m+1$. Since
$L_{\mathrm{sc}}H\le n\le(L_{\mathrm{sc}}+1)H$ and $H,m\ge1$,
\eqref{bridge:calibrated-summary} gives
\[
 \mathbb{E}\mathcal{W}_{A_B}
 \le C_1\{n^Q\log(2n)+m+1+n\}
 \le C\{H^Q\log(2+H)+m\}.
\]
head: environment

label: br5:local-inputs
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{br5:local-inputs}
For each fixed $D_{\sharp}>0$, there are computable constants $h_0,c_0>0$,
$C_{\mathrm{Hol}}<\infty$ and a positive dyadic exponent
$\alpha\in(0,1]$, depending only on $D_{\sharp}$ and the coefficient bounds,
with the following properties. For every integer $n\ge1$ and every
edge satisfying \eqref{br5:moderate},
\[
 \mathbb{E} Y_n(e)=\frac{p(e)}{g(e)},\qquad
 \frac12\le Y_n(e)\le\frac32\quad\hbox{almost surely}.
\]
Consequently, $\operatorname{SharpCoin}_n(e)$ has mean
$p(e)/(2g(e))\in[1/4,3/4]$ and uniformly bounded expected work.
With $\rho=c_0\sqrt h/(1+\sqrt n)$ and
$|u'-u|,|v'-v|\le\rho/4$, we have
\begin{equation}\label{br5:relative-holder}
 \left|\frac{p(s,u';t,v')}{p(s,u;t,v)}-1\right|
 \le C_{\mathrm{Hol}}
 \left\{\left(\frac{|u'-u|}{\rho}\right)^\alpha
       +\left(\frac{|v'-v|}{\rho}\right)^\alpha\right\}.
\end{equation}
The exponent $\alpha$ may be fixed from the coefficient bounds alone,
independently of $D_{\sharp}$.
head: environment
name: Local inputs

title: Proof
body_md:
We first bound the estimator in \eqref{br5:sharp-estimator}.
Decrease $h_0$ so that
\[
 h_0\le\min\{1,h_{\mathrm{env}},r_{\mathrm{sh}},r_{\mathrm{sh}}^2/[16(1+D_{\sharp})]\}.
\]
The moderate-displacement condition implies $|u-v|\le r_n/4$.
The known Lipschitz bound
$\|a(q,z)-a(t,v)\|_F\le L_a(|t-q|+|z-v|)$ and the choices of
$r_{\mathrm{sh}},\eta_{\mathrm{sh}}$ then imply
\begin{equation*}
 (1-\eta/4)A\preceq a(q,z)\preceq(1+\eta/4)A,
 \qquad q\in[s,t],\quad |z-v|\le r_n.
\end{equation*}

For subedges of duration $\delta$ with both endpoints in this ball,
the explicit formulas in parametrix expansion imply that
\begin{equation*}
 g\le C_1G_{V_{\mathrm{in}},\delta},\qquad
 |H|\le C_2\eta^{-3/2}\delta^{-1/2}
              G_{V_{\mathrm{in}},\delta},
\end{equation*}
where $C_1,C_2$ are computable class constants. 
For the whole input edge,
\begin{equation*}
 \frac{G_{V_{\mathrm{in}},h}(v-u)}{g(e)}
 \le\exp\{\eta D_{\sharp}n/(2\lambda)\}
 \le C_D:=\exp\{\eta_{\mathrm{sh}}D_{\sharp}/(2\lambda)\}.
\end{equation*}

Write $K_j=g\otimes H^{\otimes j}$ and split its integral into
$K_j^{\mathrm{in}}$ and $K_j^{\mathrm{out}}$ according to
$\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal I^c$. Cancellation of the gap and Gaussian
bridge densities, exactly as in \eqref{core:Tnproperties}, gives
\[
 \mathbb{E} U_j^{\mathrm{in}}
   =\frac{K_j^{\mathrm{in}}}{G_{V_{\mathrm{in}},h}(v-u)},
 \qquad
 \mathbb{E} U_j^{\mathrm{out}}
   =\frac{K_j^{\mathrm{out}}}{G_{V_{\mathrm{out}},h}(v-u)}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 |U_j^{\mathrm{in}}|
 \le C_1(C_2\eta^{-3/2})^j\mathsf Z_j(h).
\]
For an outside path, some node $z_l$ satisfies $|z_l-v|>r_n$. Hence
\[
 \sum_{i=0}^j\frac{|z_{i+1}-z_i|^2}{\Delta_i}
 \ge\frac{(|z_l-u|+|v-z_l|)^2}{h}
 \ge\frac{(7r_n/4)^2}{h}.
\]
Combining this with Lemma~\ref{core:parametrix} and
$G_{\kappa,\delta}/G_{2\kappa,\delta}
=2^{d/2}\exp\{-|z|^2/(4\kappa\delta)\}$ yields
\begin{equation*}
 |U_j^{\mathrm{out}}|
 \le C_g2^{d/2}(2^{d/2}C_H)^j\mathsf Z_j(h)
          \exp\{-c_{\mathrm{out}}r_n^2/h\},
 \qquad c_{\mathrm{out}}:=49/(64\kappa).
\end{equation*}

The absolute convolution bounds from the parametrix expansion justify
summing these expectations, so \eqref{br5:sharp-estimator} is unbiased
for $p(e)/g(e)$.
Choose $h_0$ small enough that
$2C_2\eta_{\mathrm{sh}}^{-3/2}\sqrt{\pi h_0}\le1/2$ and
$2^{1+d/2}C_H\sqrt{\pi h_0}\le1/2$.
Since $\Gamma(1+j/2)\ge1/2$, then for every $j\ge1$ the absolute inside
correction in \eqref{br5:sharp-estimator} is at most
$4C_1C_D C_2\eta_{\mathrm{sh}}^{-3/2}\sqrt{\pi h_0}$,
and the outside correction has absolute value at most
\[
 2^{d+2}C_gC_H\sqrt{\pi h}
 \exp\left\{\left(\frac{D_{\sharp}}{2\lambda}
                   -\frac{c_{\mathrm{out}}r_{\mathrm{sh}}^2}{h_0}\right)n\right\}.
\]
Decreasing $h_0$ further makes both bounds at most $1/4$, uniformly
for $n\ge1$. 
Thus $1/2\le Y_n(e)\le3/2$ and the uniform comparison has the
claimed mean. Gap generation, Gaussian bridge simulation, ball tests,
coefficient queries and evaluation of the normalizer recurrence cost
$O(j+1)$ at order $j$. Since $\mathbb{E} J_1=\mathbb{E} J_2=2$, the total expected
work is uniformly bounded. 

We prove \eqref{br5:relative-holder} with the dyadic choice
$\alpha=1/2$. In terminal variables,
\begin{equation*}
 \partial_t p=\operatorname{div}
 \left[\tfrac12a\nabla p+
       \{\tfrac12\operatorname{div}a-b\}p\right],
\end{equation*}
while the reversed backward operator is
$\operatorname{div}(\tfrac12a\nabla)
+(b-\tfrac12\operatorname{div}a)\cdot\nabla$.
The principal matrix is Lipschitz and the lower-order coefficients
are bounded, with known class bounds.

These bounds give an effective local spatial $1/2$-H\"older estimate.
Indeed, write $Q_r(q,z)=(q-r^2,q]\times B_r(z)$.
For a solution $f$ bounded by $M$ on $Q_{4R}$, $R\le1$, define
$\mathcal E(r)=\inf_c\int_{Q_r}|f-c|^2$ for centers in $Q_R$.
Then by Caccioppoli's inequality on $Q_{2r}$ and the comparison with the
constant-coefficient heat equation on $Q_r$, we have
\[
 \mathcal E(\theta r)
 \le C_1\theta^{d+4}\mathcal E(r)+C_2M^2r^{d+4},
 \qquad r\le R,\quad 0<\theta\le\tfrac14,
\]
uniformly over these centers. The constants are computable from
the energy inequalities and derivatives of the explicit Gaussian
kernel. Choose a dyadic $\theta$ with $C_1\theta\le1/2$.
Iteration gives $\mathcal E(r)\le CM^2r^{d+3}/R$; telescoping
cylinder averages then yields
$|f(q,z)-f(q,z')|\le CM(|z-z'|/R)^{1/2}$
on the smaller cylinder, including its upper time face.

Now take $c_0=1/8$ and $\rho=c_0\sqrt h/(1+\sqrt n)$.
Use endpoint cylinders of radius $4\rho$ and depth $16\rho^2$,
ending at $t$ and at $s$ in reversed time, respectively.
Their transition durations lie in $[h/2,h]$.
Decrease $h_0$ so that the preceding sharp comparison also holds
with displacement threshold $D_*=4(\sqrt{D_{\sharp}}+5)^2$.
For every edge $e'$ in these cylinders, including a displacement
of the opposite endpoint by at most $\rho/4$, the Gaussian formula
and the Lipschitz bound on $a$ give
\[
 \left|\log\frac{g(e')}{g(e)}\right|
 \le C\left\{\sqrt{n/h}\,\rho+n\rho^2/h+n(\rho+\rho^2)\right\}
 \le C.
\]
Thus $\tfrac12g\le p\le\tfrac32g$ bounds the density on both
cylinders by $Cp(e)$. Applying the local estimate successively
to the two endpoints and dividing by $p(e)>0$ proves
\eqref{br5:relative-holder}. All constants are computable from
the stated bounds. 

For $k=1$, the same conclusion follows by smooth approximation.
Extend $a$ and $b$ beyond the time interval while preserving
uniform ellipticity and controlled first-order bounds, and
mollify the extensions to obtain smooth coefficients
$a_\varepsilon,b_\varepsilon$. These approximations converge
locally uniformly to $a,b$, and the estimates above hold with
constants independent of $\varepsilon$. The corresponding
parametrix kernels converge term by term and satisfy uniform
Gaussian bounds, which provide summable, integrable majorants.
Dominated convergence therefore yields convergence of the
transition densities $p_\varepsilon$ to $p$ for $s<t$.
Passing to the limit in the density comparisons and the relative
Hölder estimate proves the result for the original coefficients.

label: br5:dag
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{br5:dag}
For the graph of Section~\ref{br5:weighted}, suppose that the edge
coins have uniformly bounded conditional expected work. The specified
procedure terminates almost surely and samples a path with probability
proportional to $\prod_{\mathfrak e\in\gamma}k_{\mathfrak e}w_{\mathfrak e}$. Its expected scalar work is
$O\{EN^3\log(4EN)\}$, uniformly in the positive factors and the total
path weight.
head: environment
name: Sampling a weighted graph path

title: Proof
body_md:
The accepted geometric proposal defining $J$ has mass
$\rho_0^j/(jC_0)$. The multiplier $8/7$ is admissible because
$(1-w_{\mathfrak e})/\rho_0\le6/7$, and
\[
 \mathbb{E} D_{\mathfrak e}=\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{\rho_0^j}{jC_0}
       \left(\frac{1-w_{\mathfrak e}}{\rho_0}\right)^j
       =-\frac{\log w_{\mathfrak e}}{C_0}.
\]
Hence the stated mixture returns a $c_{\mathfrak e}$-coin. Both the geometric
rejection loop and its accepted count have bounded means, proving
the uniform work bound for this transformation. The factory's scalar
work assertion includes its geometric inner loops: when its multiplier
belongs to a fixed compact subset of $(1,\infty)$, their means remain
uniformly bounded. Each outer update follows a nonempty inner loop
and uses fixed scalar work, including powers evaluated by exponentials
and logarithms.

Condition on the initial estimates $(\widehat c_{\mathfrak e})_{\mathfrak e}$ and denote
\[
 R_\gamma=L_0\sum_{\mathfrak e\in\gamma}(c_{\mathfrak e}-\widehat c_{\mathfrak e}),\qquad
 v_\gamma=\frac12+R_\gamma/\lambda_0,\qquad
 v_* =\max_\gamma v_\gamma.
\]
The proposal law is proportional to
$\prod_{\mathfrak e\in\gamma}k_{\mathfrak e}\exp\{L_0(\widehat c_{\mathfrak e}-1)\}$.
For fresh edge estimates $(\overline c_{\mathfrak e})_{\mathfrak e}$, let
$z_* =\mathbb{E}(\widehat v_*\mid\text{initial estimates})$.
It is common to all proposed paths, and a factor coin has mean
$1+v_\gamma-z_*$.
Jensen's inequality gives $z_*\ge v_*$.
Hoeffding's inequality and the choice of $B_0$ imply
\[
 \mathbb{P}\!\left(\max_{\mathfrak e}|\overline c_{\mathfrak e}-c_{\mathfrak e}|>1/\lambda_0
                 \mid\text{initial estimates}\right)
 \le (2\lambda_0)^{-1}.
\]
On its complement every empirical path error is at most
$1/(2\lambda_0)$, and errors are always at most one. Consequently
$0\le z_*-v_*\le1/\lambda_0$.
The factors use independent sets of edge estimates and fresh uniform
variables. Averaging their product over the Poisson count gives
\[
 A_\gamma
 =\exp\{\lambda_0(v_\gamma-z_*)\}
 =\exp\{\lambda_0(1/2-z_*)\}\exp(R_\gamma).
\]
The first factor is common to all candidate paths. Multiplying this
acceptance probability by the proposal weight therefore gives a
common multiple of $\prod_{\mathfrak e\in\gamma}k_{\mathfrak e}w_{\mathfrak e}$. This proves the exact
path law for every realization of the initial estimates.

To bound retries, let
$\mathcal G=\{\max_{\mathfrak e}|\widehat c_{\mathfrak e}-c_{\mathfrak e}|\le(NL_0)^{-1}\}$.
The choice of $J_0$ gives
$\mathbb{P}(\mathcal G^c)\le e^{-\lambda_0}$.
On $\mathcal G$, all $R_\gamma\in[-1,1]$; their range is always
at most $\lambda_0$. If $a_{\rm init}$ is the mean acceptance
conditional on the initial estimates, then we have
\[
 a_{\rm init}\ge e^{-\lambda_0-1},\qquad
 a_{\rm init}\ge e^{-3}\ \text{on }\mathcal G,
 \qquad \mathbb{E}(a_{\rm init}^{-1})\le e^3+e.
\]
Each empirical factor costs $O(EB_0)$ expected work uniformly in
the initial estimates and candidate path. The Poisson loop uses
mean $\lambda_0+1$ exponential increments, including the overshoot,
so one trial costs $O\{EN^3\log(4EN)\}$.
Generating the initial estimates costs
$O\{EN^2(N+\log E)\}$ and is of no larger order.
Conditional on the initial estimates, the trial records are
independent and identically distributed.
Lemma~\ref{supp:fw:retry}, followed by averaging the bound on
$a_{\rm init}^{-1}$, finishes the proof.

label: br5:density-bounds
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Density bounds for the bridge construction

title: Proof
body_md:
For the lower bound, choose a fixed
$0<\delta\le\min\{h(1),h_{\mathrm{env}},1/2\}$ from
Lemma~\ref{core:localpositive}, and let
\[
 a_*=\tfrac34(2\pi\Lambda\delta)^{-d/2}e^{-1/(16\lambda)}.
\]
Choose a radius $r_*>0$ so that
$r_*\le\sqrt\delta/8$ and the cube
$K=[-r_*/\sqrt d,r_*/\sqrt d]^d$ has volume $v_*\le1/(2a_*)$.
For endpoints
in $K$ and $\delta/2\le\tau\le\delta$, we have
$|v-u|\le2r_*$ and $|v-u|^2/\tau\le1/8$.
Lemma~\ref{core:localpositive} therefore gives
$p\ge3g/4\ge a_*$. Partition
$T_0=2n$ into $M=\lceil T_0/\delta\rceil$ equal durations. They
belong to $[\delta/2,\delta]$, and Chapman--Kolmogorov identity restricted to
$K$ at the internal times implies
\[
 p_{T_0}\ge a_*^M v_*^{M-1}
   =a_*(a_*v_*)^{M-1}\ge c_*e^{-C_*n}.
\]
For example, $c_*=a_*$ and
$C_*=(4/\delta)|\log(a_*v_*)|$ suffice.
For the upper bound, fix $0<\delta'\le h_{\mathrm{env}}$ and a
transition of duration at least $\delta'$. Split off a final interval
of length $\delta'$, use $p\le K_{\mathrm b}G_{c,\delta'}$ there,
and integrate the preceding transition probability. If the whole
duration equals $\delta'$, apply the short-time bound directly.
Thus one may take
$\delta_*=h_{\mathrm{env}}$ and
$C_{\mathrm{den}}=K_{\mathrm b}(2\pi c)^{-d/2}$.

label: br5:cell-comparison
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{br5:cell-comparison}
The preceding calibration implies \eqref{br5:cell-errors} and
\eqref{br5:cell-slack}. All sharp-coin calls on good cell edges,
including actual endpoints, satisfy \eqref{br5:moderate}.
head: environment
name: Comparison within cells

title: Proof
body_md:
An endpoint differs from its center by at most $\sqrt d\ell/2$,
which is at most $\rho/4$ by \eqref{br5:cell-choice}. The relative
H\"older estimate therefore bounds the density error by
\[
 2C_{\mathrm{Hol}}(\sqrt d c_1/2)^\alpha N^{-1}
 \le(100N)^{-1}.
\]
Also $\sqrt d\ell/L\le\sqrt d c_1c_0/(2\sqrt D)\le1/4$.
Hence both the center edge and every actual edge in its cells have
displacement at most $5L/4$, within the calibrated threshold
$D_{\sharp}$.

For the frozen Gaussian, differentiate its log density along the
segment joining the center endpoints to the actual endpoints. Every
intermediate edge remains within the calibrated displacement threshold.
The covariance derivative bound and ellipticity bound the derivative
along this segment by $C_G\sqrt{n/h}$ times the maximum endpoint
displacement, with $C_G$ as chosen above. Thus
\[
 \left|\log\frac{g(e)}{g(e^0)}\right|
 \le \frac{\sqrt d\ell}{2}C_G\sqrt{n/h}
 \le\frac{\sqrt d c_1c_0C_G}{2N}
 \le\frac1{600N}.
\]
Here $h\le n^{-3}$ controls covariance-derivative terms, and
$N^{-1/\alpha}\le N^{-1}$. Exponentiating yields the second
inequality in \eqref{br5:cell-errors}. Finally, for the graph edge
$\mathfrak e$ corresponding to the actual transition $e$,
\[
 \frac{1+1/(10N)}{1+1/(100N)}
 \le\frac{U_{\mathfrak e}}{p(e)}
 \le\frac{1+1/(10N)}{1-1/(100N)}.
\]
The bounds \eqref{br5:cell-slack} follow by direct subtraction of one.
head: environment

label: br5:ratio
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{br5:ratio}
The race returns a $p(e)/U_{\mathfrak e}$-coin with expected work $O(N)$,
uniformly over good edges and endpoints in their cells. Applying
these coins independently conditional on the states to all $N$
edges gives one cell-component trial with accepted density
$F\mathbf{1}_{E_0}/Z_0$. The uniform state draws and acceptance tests
have total expected work $O(N^2)$, uniformly in the selected path.
head: environment
name: Acceptance within cells

title: Proof
body_md:
The cell errors \eqref{br5:cell-errors} imply
$9/10\le\beta\le1$, so $2\beta$ stays in a fixed compact subset
of $(1,\infty)$. Also $A=\beta q\le q_0\le3/4$, making the first
factory admissible with gap $1/4$. More precisely,
\[
 \frac{A}{q_0}=\frac{p(e)}{U_{\mathfrak e}}
 \le\frac{1+1/(100N)}{1+1/(10N)}
 =\frac{100N+1}{100N+10},
\]
and therefore
\[
 q_0-A\ge\frac14\frac9{100N+10}
 \ge\frac9{440N}>\frac1{50N}.
\]
The multiplier-two factory is thus admissible with its stated gap,
and its complement has mean $q_0-A$ and expected work $O(N)$.
Each race trial succeeds with probability
$(A+q_0-A)/2=q_0/2\ge1/8$. Conditional on success, its label is
$A$ with probability $A/q_0=p(e)/U_{\mathfrak e}$. A trial has expected work
$O(N)$, so Lemma~\ref{supp:fw:retry} gives the same order for the
complete race. This argument permits dependence between a trial's
work and its success bit.

For the cell component, let $e_i$ be the actual transition represented
by graph edge $\mathfrak e_i$ of the selected path. Multiplying its
proposal density by the fresh acceptance probabilities gives
\[
 \frac{\prod_i U_{\mathfrak e_i}}{Z_0}
 \prod_i\frac{p(e_i)}{U_{\mathfrak e_i}}\mathbf{1}_{E_0}
 =\frac{F\mathbf{1}_{E_0}}{Z_0}.
\]
For every selected path and every choice of states in its cells,
\eqref{br5:cell-slack} bounds the acceptance probability below by
$(1+C_2/N)^{-N}\ge e^{-C_2}$. Uniform state generation costs
$O(N)$, and the $N$ fresh acceptance coins cost $O(N^2)$ in expectation.
head: environment

label: br5:residual-guarantee
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{br5:residual-guarantee}
Every comparison in the bad-edge and exit constructions is valid on
its retained event. Their one-trial accepted subdensities are,
respectively,
$F\mathbf{1}_{B_i}/D_i$ and $F\mathbf{1}_{X_\zeta}/D_\zeta$. A bad-edge trial
has expected work $O(N+NS_{\mathrm{cell}})$, and an exit trial has
expected work $O(N+n+NS_{\mathrm{cell}})$, uniformly in its label.
head: environment
name: Bad-edge and exit components

title: Proof
body_md:
We first verify that the first-violation classification has finite
work. Before a violation occurs, the current state lies in a box
cell, or is the initial state. Enumerate all cells whose coordinate
indices have absolute value at most
$J_{\mathrm{box}}+\lceil L/\ell\rceil+1$.
This finite collection contains every good neighbor of a box cell.
Thus a proposed next state outside this collection creates a bad edge.
Otherwise, a finite scan locates its half-open cell and determines
whether the edge is bad and whether the state lies outside the box.
The bad-edge test is performed first, as in the main construction,
and the scan stops at the first violation.
Writing $S_{\mathrm{cell}}$ for the number of box cells, this collection
contains $O(S_{\mathrm{cell}})$ cells. Classification therefore costs
$O(NS_{\mathrm{cell}})$ work.

For a bad-edge component $B_i$, recall that a bad edge has actual
displacement greater than $3L/4$, since $\sqrt d\ell\le L/4$.
The Gaussian formula and the definition of $\delta_J$ imply
\[
 K_{\mathrm b}G_{c,h}(w)\le\delta_JG_{2c,h}(w)
 \qquad\text{on every bad edge}.
\]
Also, both $K_{\mathrm b}G_{c,h}$ and $G_{2c,h}$ are bounded by
$Q_h$, using $K_{\mathrm b}\ge1$.
These inequalities verify that the known comparison probabilities
in the bad-edge construction lie in $[0,1]$ on the retained event.

For $i<N$, the proposal density before classification is
\[
 G_{2c,h}(w_i)\prod_{\substack{1\le j<N\\j\ne i}}p_j.
\]
Conditional on the proposed states, the transition coin and uniform
comparison on edge $i$ jointly succeed with probability
\[
 \frac{p_i}{K_{\mathrm b}G_{c,h}(w_i)}
 \frac{K_{\mathrm b}G_{c,h}(w_i)}
      {\delta_JG_{2c,h}(w_i)}
 =\frac{p_i}{\delta_JG_{2c,h}(w_i)}.
\]
The two tests on the last edge jointly succeed with probability
$p_N/Q_h$.
Multiplying these probabilities by the proposal density and the
classification indicator gives
$F\mathbf{1}_{B_i}/(\delta_JQ_h)=F\mathbf{1}_{B_i}/D_i$.
For $i=N$, the proposal density is $\prod_{j<N}p_j$, and the two
last-edge tests jointly succeed with probability
$p_N/(\delta_JQ_h)$ on $B_N$, giving the same identity.
Each bad-edge proposal trial has expected work
$O(N+NS_{\mathrm{cell}})$.

We next consider an exit component $X_\zeta$.
The proposal uses drift $b+a\theta$ until the first coarse-grid
observation outside $\mathcal B$, and drift $b$ thereafter.
By the product rule, derivatives of $a_{ij}$ of total order
$r\le k$ are bounded by $d2^r\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}}^2$.
This proves the enlarged coefficient bound stated in the main text.
Since the diffusion coefficient is unchanged, the original
ellipticity bounds also hold. The short-transition sampler therefore
applies in each drift regime, using only original coefficient
value queries.

Keep the main-text convention $\tau=\infty$ when no coarse-grid
exit occurs, and define $\bar\tau=\tau\wedge(T_0-h).$
Write $\mathbb Q_\theta$ for the law of the proposal process through
$T_0-h$. The time $\bar\tau$ is a bounded stopping time.
Boundedness of $\sigma^\top\theta$ gives Novikov's condition, so
Girsanov's theorem yields the likelihood of the original unconditional diffusion law through $T_0-h$, relative to $\mathbb Q_\theta$:
\begin{equation*}
 \mathcal L
 =\exp\left\{
   -\theta\cdot X_{\bar\tau}
   +\int_0^{\bar\tau}V(t,X_t)\,\mathrm{d} t
 \right\}.
\end{equation*}

On the retained event $X_\zeta$, we have $\bar\tau=\tau$,
$\theta\cdot X_\tau\ge B\ge R_-$ and $V_-\le V\le V_+$.
Consequently, $\mathcal L\le\delta_X$ and
\[
 \frac{\mathcal L}{\delta_X}
 =e^{-\theta\cdot X_\tau+R_-}
  e^{V_+(\tau-T_0)}
  \exp\left\{\int_0^\tau
       (V(t,X_t)-V_+)\,\mathrm{d} t\right\}.
\]
The first two factors are implemented by the two one-time uniform
comparisons in \eqref{br5:exit-tests}.
Conditionally on the full proposal path, the probability that all
comparisons at the independent Poisson times before $\tau$ succeed is
\[
 \exp\left\{
 \int_0^\tau q_V
 \left(\frac{V(t,X_t)-V_-}{q_V}-1\right)\,\mathrm{d} t
 \right\}
 =
 \exp\left\{\int_0^\tau
       (V(t,X_t)-V_+)\,\mathrm{d} t\right\}.
\]
Thus these Poisson comparisons implement the remaining factor.

Simulation at the merged times has exactly the joint law used in
this calculation. To see this, first consider a full proposal
process and an independent Poisson process, then observe the
proposal process at the merged times. The drift switches only at
the first coarse-grid exit, so observing additional states at
Poisson times does not change its law.
The exact short-transition sampler generates these observations
with the required joint distribution.
The comparisons in \eqref{br5:exit-tests} therefore implement
$\mathcal L/\delta_X$ after averaging over the auxiliary observations.
The final transition coin and uniform comparison jointly have mean
$p_N/Q_h$. Applying change of measure and integrating out the
auxiliary observations gives the accepted density
\[
 \frac{F\mathbf{1}_{X_\zeta}}{\delta_XQ_h}
 =\frac{F\mathbf{1}_{X_\zeta}}{D_\zeta}.
\]

The expected number of Poisson times is $q_V(T_0-h)=O(n)$.
Their generation includes the overshooting exponential draw, and
merging the two ordered time grids costs $O(N+n)$ in expectation.
Every merged gap is at most $h$, so each transition has uniformly
bounded conditional expected work under the active drift.
Potential evaluations and uniform comparisons cost $O(n)$ in
expectation. Including classification, one exit proposal trial
therefore has expected work
$O(N+n+NS_{\mathrm{cell}})$.

label: br5:global-guarantee
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{br5:global-guarantee}
One complete trial, consisting of an augmented-graph draw and the
selected component's proposal and acceptance test, has accepted
density $F/M_{\mathrm{env}}$,
where $M_{\mathrm{env}}\le Cp_{T_0}$. Its expected work is at most
\[
 C\{E_{\mathrm{aug}}N^3\log(4E_{\mathrm{aug}}N)
        +N^2+n+NS_{\mathrm{cell}}\},
\]
where $E_{\mathrm{aug}}$ is the number of augmented-graph edges.
Independent complete retries return an exact coarse bridge and
increase this bound by at most a class constant.
head: environment
name: The coarse bridge trial

title: Proof
body_md:
Lemma~\ref{br5:dag} selects an original cell path or an auxiliary
component path proportionally to its weight. Thus it chooses the
cell component with probability $Z_0/M_{\mathrm{env}}$, a bad-edge
component with probability $D_i/M_{\mathrm{env}}$, and an exit
component with probability $D_\zeta/M_{\mathrm{env}}$. Conditional
on selecting the cell component, it also gives the required cell-path
law. The subsequent proposals and acceptance tests use fresh
randomness. Lemmas~\ref{br5:ratio} and~\ref{br5:residual-guarantee}
therefore imply one-trial accepted density
\[
 \frac{Z_0}{M_{\mathrm{env}}}
       \frac{F\mathbf{1}_{E_0}}{Z_0}
 +\sum_{i=1}^N
       \frac{D_i}{M_{\mathrm{env}}}
       \frac{F\mathbf{1}_{B_i}}{D_i}
 +\sum_\zeta
       \frac{D_\zeta}{M_{\mathrm{env}}}
       \frac{F\mathbf{1}_{X_\zeta}}{D_\zeta}
 =\frac{F}{M_{\mathrm{env}}},
\]
because $E_0$, the $B_i$ and the $X_\zeta$ partition skeleton space.
The bad-edge test takes priority at the first violation, so none of
these events overlap.

We next bound the total envelope mass. By the definitions of the
residual masses,
\[
 M_{\mathrm{env}}=Z_0+N\delta_JQ_h+2d\delta_XQ_h.
\]
Let $p_{T_0}=p(0,0;T_0,0)$ and use
$p_{T_0}\ge c_*e^{-C_*n}$.
The choices in \eqref{br5:insertion-constants} give
$9D/(64c)>C_*$ and $R_0>2V_++C_*$, while
\eqref{br5:cell-choice} gives $\ell\le1$ and $R_->0$.
Since $N\asymp n^4$, $h\asymp n^{-3}$ and
$R_-=R_0(n+1)-\ell/2$, we obtain
\[
 \frac{N\delta_JQ_h}{p_{T_0}}
 \le Cn^{4+3d/2}
       e^{-[9D/(64c)-C_*]n}
 \le C,
 \qquad
 \frac{2d\delta_XQ_h}{p_{T_0}}
 \le Cn^{3d/2}
       e^{-[R_0-2V_+-C_*]n}
 \le C.
\]
The within-cell bound also implies
\[
 Z_0
 \le (1+C_2/N)^N\int_{E_0}F
 \le e^{C_2}p_{T_0}.
\]
Therefore $M_{\mathrm{env}}\le Cp_{T_0}$, uniformly in $n$ and
the coefficients within the class.
Each complete trial succeeds with probability
$p_{T_0}/M_{\mathrm{env}}\ge C^{-1}$.
Conditional on success, its density is
\[
 \frac{F/M_{\mathrm{env}}}{p_{T_0}/M_{\mathrm{env}}}
 =\frac{F}{p_{T_0}},
\]
the exact coarse-bridge density.

For completeness, the work of one trial includes the augmented
graph draw as well as the selected component's proposal and tests.
Let $E_{\mathrm{aug}}$ be the number of edges in the augmented graph.
The original edge coins have uniformly bounded expected work,
and the auxiliary edge coins return one deterministically.
Lemma~\ref{br5:dag} therefore bounds the expected work of the graph
draw, including its initial estimates and internal retries, by
$O\{E_{\mathrm{aug}}N^3\log(4E_{\mathrm{aug}}N)\}$.
The within-cell proposal and acceptance tests cost $O(N^2)$ in expectation,
uniformly over the selected original graph path.
The bad-edge and exit trial bounds proved above consequently give
the following uniform bound for one complete trial:
\[
 c_{\mathrm{trial}}
 =C\left\{
 E_{\mathrm{aug}}N^3\log(4E_{\mathrm{aug}}N)
 +N^2+n+NS_{\mathrm{cell}}
 \right\}.
\]

After a failed trial, the algorithm restarts the augmented graph
draw with fresh initial estimates and fresh component randomness.
Thus complete trials are independent and identically distributed
for fixed coefficients and calibrated graph.
Lemma~\ref{supp:fw:retry} bounds the expected work through the first
success by
\[
 c_{\mathrm{trial}}\frac{M_{\mathrm{env}}}{p_{T_0}}
 \le Cc_{\mathrm{trial}}.
\]
The one-time graph construction cost is accounted for separately
in Section~\ref{br5:bridge-sampler-proof}.

label: br5:insertion
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{br5:insertion}
Starting from an exact coarse bridge, the procedure of
Section~\ref{br5:insert-section} inserts all requested times with
the exact joint bridge law and terminates almost surely. Its expected
additional work is $O(m+N)$, uniformly in $n$, the coefficient class
and the requested spacings. Each insertion, once its neighboring
states are identified, has uniformly bounded expected sampling work
under their bridge law.
head: environment
name: Insertion work

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix an insertion time and condition on the retained states.
Write $p_i=p(e_i)$, and first suppose that
$|v-u|^2/h'\le D_0n$.
On $S_0$, the covariance of the first frozen kernel differs from
$A=a(r,v)$ by at most
\[
 \|a(t,z)-A\|_F
 \le L_a\{h'+\sqrt{D_1nh'}\}
 \le\frac{L_a\{h_0+\sqrt{D_1h_0}\}}{n}
 \le\frac1{2n}.
\]
The second frozen covariance is $A$.
Both are therefore bounded above by $A_+=A+I_d/n$.
Ellipticity and $A_+\preceq(\Lambda+1)I_d$ give
\[
 g(e_1)\le C_g'G_{A_+,\tau_1}(z-u),
 \qquad
 g(e_2)\le C_g'G_{A_+,\tau_2}(v-z).
\]
Moreover, $\tau_i\le h\le h_0n^{-3}$, and the displacement
conditions defining $S_0$ make both sharp-coin calls admissible.
Thus the two sharp coins and the two uniform comparisons have
product mean $p_1p_2/\mathcal E_0(z)$.

On $S_1$,
\[
 \frac{K_{\mathrm b}G_{c,\tau_1}(z-u)}
      {\delta_1G_{2c,\tau_1}(z-u)}
 =
 \exp\left\{\frac{D_1n-|z-u|^2/\tau_1}{4c}\right\}
 \le1.
\]
Combining this comparison with the two transition coins gives
mean $p_1p_2/\mathcal E_1(z)$.
The calculation on $S_2$ is identical for the second subinterval.
Since the sets $S_j$ partition $\mathbb{R}^d$, choosing component $j$
with probability $M_j/(M_0+M_1+M_2)$ and then applying its tests
gives the one-trial accepted density
\[
 \frac{p(s,u;t,z)p(t,z;r,v)}{M_0+M_1+M_2},
\]
which has mass $p(s,u;r,v)/(M_0+M_1+M_2)$, and conditioning on
acceptance gives the required conditional bridge density.

We next bound the expected work of these mixture trials.
Covariance comparison gives
\[
 \frac{G_{A_+,h'}(v-u)}{g(s,u;r,v)}
 \le
 \exp\left\{\frac{|v-u|^2}{2\lambda^2nh'}\right\}
 \le e^{D_0/(2\lambda^2)},
\]
so $M_0\le Cg(s,u;r,v)$.
The Gaussian covariances in $M_1$ and $M_2$ lie between
$ch'I_d$ and $2ch'I_d$. Hence
\[
 M_1+M_2
 \le C\exp\left\{
       \left[-\frac{D_1}{4c}+\frac{D_0}{2\lambda}\right]n
       \right\}
       g(s,u;r,v)
 \le Cg(s,u;r,v).
\]
Here \eqref{br5:insertion-constants} makes the exponent negative.
The existing edge also satisfies the conditions of
Lemma~\ref{br5:local-inputs}, which gives
$p(s,u;r,v)\ge\tfrac12g(s,u;r,v)$.
Thus $M_0+M_1+M_2\le Cp(s,u;r,v)$, so each mixture trial has
a uniformly positive success probability.

The Gaussian draws, matrix operations, uniform comparisons and
coin calls have uniformly bounded expected work in fixed dimension.
Throughout retries, the existing states and insertion time remain
fixed, while the mixture index, candidate state and acceptance
randomness are regenerated independently.
Lemma~\ref{supp:fw:retry} therefore gives uniformly bounded
conditional expected sampling work for moderate endpoints.

For $|v-u|^2/h'>D_0n$, the Gaussian bridge proposal has density
\[
 \frac{G_{c,\tau_1}(z-u)G_{c,\tau_2}(v-z)}{G_{c,h'}(v-u)}.
\]
The two transition coins give accepted density
$p_1p_2/(K_{\mathrm b}^2G_{c,h'}(v-u))$.
This again yields the required conditional bridge law.
Each trial has uniformly bounded conditional expected work, so
Lemma~\ref{supp:fw:retry} bounds the conditional expected sampling
work by
\[
 C\frac{G_{c,h'}(v-u)}{p(s,u;r,v)}.
\]
The fixed preliminary operations can be absorbed into this bound,
since $p(s,u;r,v)\le K_{\mathrm b}G_{c,h'}(v-u)$.
For every fixed pair of endpoints, the acceptance probability is
positive, so this insertion also terminates almost surely.

It remains to average the last cost on the large-displacement
event. Each successful insertion preserves the joint bridge law,
by the conditional-density calculations above.
The times $s,r$ are deterministic functions of the requested
grid and coarse grid; they do not depend on the sampled states.
Writing $T_0=2n$ and $p_{T_0}=p(0,0;T_0,0)$, their bridge marginal
therefore gives the expected large-displacement contribution
\begin{equation}\label{br5:insertion-cancel}
 \frac{C}{p_{T_0}}\iint
 p(0,0;s,u)G_{c,h'}(v-u)
 \mathbf{1}_{\{|v-u|^2/h'>D_0n\}}
 p(r,v;T_0,0)\,\,\mathrm{d} u\,\,\mathrm{d} v.
\end{equation}
Here the factor $p(s,u;r,v)$ in the endpoint marginal cancels
the denominator of the conditional work bound.
At $s=0$, the first transition measure is a point mass at zero;
at $r=T_0$, the final endpoint is fixed at zero.

If $r<T_0$, then $r$ is a right coarse endpoint and
$T_0-r\ge h$.
By \eqref{br5:global-density}, the last density in
\eqref{br5:insertion-cancel} is at most $Ch^{-d/2}$, while
$p_{T_0}^{-1}\le Ce^{C_*n}$.
Also,
\[
 \int G_{c,h'}(w)
 \mathbf{1}_{\{|w|^2/h'>D_0n\}}\,\,\mathrm{d} w
 \le Ce^{-D_0n/(4c)}.
\]
Integrating the first transition probability therefore bounds
\eqref{br5:insertion-cancel} by
\[
 Ch^{-d/2}
 \exp\{[C_*-D_0/(4c)]n\}.
\]
This is uniformly bounded because $h\asymp n^{-3}$ and
$D_0/(4c)=C_*+1$.

If $r=T_0$, then $v=0$ and $s\ge T_0-h\ge1$.
The first density has a fixed supremum bound by
\eqref{br5:global-density}.
Integrating over $u$ and using the same Gaussian tail estimate
gives the preceding bound without the factor $h^{-d/2}$.
Thus the large-displacement contribution is uniformly bounded
in this case as well.

Combining the moderate and larger-displacement estimates shows
that each insertion, once its neighboring states are identified,
has uniformly bounded unconditional expected sampling work.
Linearity of expectation gives $O(m)$ for all such sampling work.
Merging the ordered grids, identifying neighboring states, copying
coincident states and writing the outputs requires $O(N+m)$
additional work.

title: Proof
body_md:
Theorems~\ref{fw:upper} and~\ref{bridge:general} establish admissibility
of $A_F$ and $A_B$. Since writing each requested state has positive
cost, every admissible algorithm in either family satisfies
$\mathcal{W}_A\ge c_{\mathrm{out}}m$ for a fixed $c_{\mathrm{out}}>0$.
We first establish the additional lower bound in $t_m$ for unconditional diffusion sampling.

Fix $T$, $x$, the grid and an admissible unconditional exact diffusion algorithm $A$,
and let $\tau=t_m$. Nonemptiness of $\mathcal F_T$ supplies a matrix
$\Sigma_0$ satisfying
\[
 |(\Sigma_0)_{ij}|\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}},\qquad
 \lambdaI_d\preceq\Sigma_0\Sigma_0^\top\preceq\LambdaI_d:
\]
take the value of an admissible diffusion coefficient at any one point.
The constant coefficient $\sigma(t,z)=\Sigma_0$ satisfies the same
bounds and has all positive-order derivatives zero. Set $v=(\Sigma_0\Sigma_0^\top)_{11}\le\Lambda$.

Suppose first that $\tau\ge1$ and let $N=\lfloor\tau\rfloor$.
Choose a fixed $\phi\in C_c^\infty((0,1))$ with positive integral
$\bar\phi$ and $\|\phi^{(r)}\|_\infty\le1$ for $0\le r\le k$,
extended by zero outside $(0,1)$. Such a function is obtained by
scaling any nonzero nonnegative smooth bump. Put
$\delta=\Gamma_{\mathrm{coef}}/2$ and $\mu=\delta\bar\phi>0$. For
$\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}^N$, define
\begin{equation}\label{fw:sign-family}
 b_\varepsilon(t,z)=\delta e_1
       \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\varepsilon_j\phi(t-j),\qquad
 \sigma_\varepsilon(t,z)=\Sigma_0.
\end{equation}
Here $e_1$ is the first coordinate vector. The temporal supports are
disjoint, all spatial derivatives vanish, and the drift is zero after
$N$. Thus every pair in this finite family belongs to $\mathcal F_T$.

Give the signs an independent fair prior, independently of the
algorithmic randomness. In the next calculations, expectations include
both sources of randomness. Let $S=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\varepsilon_j$,
and let $Y$ be the first coordinate of the algorithm's last output
minus $x_1$. Exactness for each member of the family gives
\begin{equation}\label{fw:sign-moments}
 Y\mid\varepsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu S,v\tau),\qquad
 \mathbb{E}[YS]=\mu N,\qquad \mathbb{E} Y^2=\mu^2N+v\tau.
\end{equation}

Represent the algorithmic randomness by an independent sequence of
the allowed uniform and Gaussian draws, called the random tape.
Fixing this sequence and the query replies determines the execution.
Only the draws actually used are charged. Since the sign family is
finite and $A$ terminates almost surely on each member, there is a
common probability-one set of tapes on which all these executions
terminate.

For the convenience of the proof, reveal $\varepsilon_j$ whenever the algorithm
first makes a coefficient query at a time in $[j,j+1)$,
$0\le j<N$. This includes queries whose actual replies do not depend
on that sign; the additional information does not change the algorithm.
Let $N_R$ be the number of signs revealed, $S_R$ their sum, and
$\mathcal H$ the sigma-field generated by the complete query record,
these revelations and the full random tape. Each revealed sign
requires a distinct coefficient query, and $Y$ is
$\mathcal H$-measurable. We claim that
\begin{equation}\label{fw:read-identities}
 \mathbb{E}[S\mid\mathcal H]=S_R,\qquad
 \mathbb{E} S_R^2=\mathbb{E} N_R.
\end{equation}
With the tape fixed, changing any unrevealed signs leaves every query
reply and hence the entire execution unchanged. Conditional on the
record and tape, these signs therefore remain independent and fair,
which proves the first identity. For the second, order the first
revelations and pad this sequence with zeros to length $N$.
Given the tape and the preceding revelations, the next previously unqueried
time interval, or termination without another revelation, is determined.
The sign in any such new interval is still independent and fair. The
padded increments consequently have conditional mean zero and are
orthogonal. Their sum is $S_R$ and their sum of squares is $N_R$,
proving the second identity. Spatially adaptive queries provide no
additional information because the coefficients in
\eqref{fw:sign-family} are independent of space.

Using \eqref{fw:sign-moments}, \eqref{fw:read-identities} and
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, we obtain
\[
 \mu^2N^2=(\mathbb{E}[YS_R])^2
 \le (\mu^2N+v\tau)\mathbb{E} N_R.
\]
Since $\tau/2\le N\le\tau$ and $v\le\Lambda$, then
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb{E} N_R\ge\frac{\mu^2N^2}{\mu^2N+v\tau}
 \ge\frac{\mu^2}{4(\mu^2+\Lambda)}\,\tau.
\end{equation*}
Each revelation requires a coefficient query with positive cost,
separate from the output writes. The average expected work over the
finite sign family is therefore at least
$c_1\tau+c_{\mathrm{out}}m$, so some deterministic member has at
least this expected work. The constants depend only on the class and
primitive costs. This argument does not require finite expected work
of $A$: its output moments in \eqref{fw:sign-moments} are finite by
exactness, and $N_R\le N$.

For $0<\tau<1$, output cost alone suffices because $\tau+m\le2m$.
Combining the two cases gives, for every admissible $A$ and every requested grid,
\begin{equation}\label{fw:fixed-grid-lower}
 \sup_{(b,\sigma)\in\mathcal F_T}
 \mathbb{E}_{b,\sigma}\mathcal{W}_A(T,x,\mathbf t)\ge c(t_m+m).
\end{equation}
Together with Theorem~\ref{fw:upper}, this also proves
fixed-grid optimality. For the grid supremum, choose
$t_i=iT/m$, so $t_m=T$. The lower bound holds for every admissible
algorithm on this grid, while Theorem~\ref{fw:upper} gives
$\mathbb{E}\mathcal{W}_{A_F}\le C(T+m)$ uniformly over all allowed grids.
Taking the infimum over algorithms proves part~(i).

For bridges, fix $T,x,y$ and write $H=H_{T,x,y}$. The output cost
gives $\mathfrak R_B^{x,y}(T,m)\ge c_{\mathrm{out}}m$.
Theorem~\ref{bridge:general} gives
\[
 \sup_{\substack{(b,\sigma)\in\mathcal F_T\\
                 \mathbf t\in\mathcal G_B(T,m)}}
 \mathbb{E}_{b,\sigma}\mathcal{W}_{A_B}(T,x,y,\mathbf t)
 \le C_B\{H^Q\log(2+H)+m\}.
\]
Since $m\ge1$, the right side is at most
$C_{T,|y-x|}m$, where one may take $C_{T,|y-x|}=C_B\{H^Q\log(2+H)+1\},$
which proves part~(ii).
